newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ad agency Tostmann & Wulfes mulls sell-off.
newsitem.headline: German ad agency Tostmann & Wulfes mulls sell-off.

text.p: The co-owner of German advertising agency Tostmann & Wulfes, Tom Tostmann, confirmed his partner, Thomas Wulfes, was considering leaving the agency and that they were discussing a possible sell-off.

"We are talking about the future," Tostmann said on Tuesday, adding he expected a final decision about Wulfes' future with the agency to be reached in the next two days. He said it was possible Wulfes would stay on as a consultant to the agency.
Tostmann said he did not plan to hold all shares in the company if Wulfes left and said he was in negotiations with international ad groups.
"We have spoken with a total of 12 international agencies about buying us out," Tostmann said. He said TBWA, AP Lintas, Young & Rubicam and McCann-Erickson were potential buyers.
Tostmann also said he recently spoke with Interpublic chief executive Phil Geier, but he said the discussions did not produce any concrete results.
Trade publication New Business reported on Monday Tostmann was considering moving to Lowe & Parters as chief executive officer.
Tostmann said Wulfes' departure the agency was based on "purely personal reasons."
Tostmann & Wulfes expect gross income for the current year to reach about 11.5 million marks ($6.4 million), up from 10.8 million marks last year. ($ = 1.791 German Marks)
